summary: Pipeline jobs stuck pending: runner provisioning label sanity-check rejects newly rotated runner tokens
description:
Issue summary:
Several release pipelines in prod became stuck in 'Pending - Waiting for runner' after the scheduled runner token rotation. New ephemeral runners register successfully but are immediately rejected by the CI scheduler because the runner label validation path rejects normalized labels when tokens include a legacy prefix.

Impact:
- Multiple release pipelines (build+e2e) blocked for the last ~2 hours, affecting two teams.
- Customer-facing deploys delayed; one internal canary was missed.

Environment:
- Prod CI cluster (us-east-1) using ephemeral GitHub Actions runners managed by runner-provisioner service.
- Secrets rotation completed at 2026-03-12T01:15:00Z via vault-rotation job.

Steps to reproduce (observed on prod):
1) Trigger typical release pipeline that requests runner with label 'release/canary-v2'.
2) Runner-provisioner spins up ephemeral instance and registers runner with token that contains rotated prefix 'rk_'.
3) CI scheduler performs label sanity-check and calls normalization routine. The routine checks token metadata and applies a legacy-path branch which strips slashes incorrectly producing 'release-canary-v2'.
4) Scheduler rejects runner because configured pool expects 'release/canary-v2' labels. Job stays pending.

Observed behavior:
- Runners show as active in provisioner logs but in CI scheduler metrics they are 'rejected_label_mismatch'.
- No 5xx errors from provisioner, but scheduler enqueues jobs without assignment.

Expected behavior:
- Normalization should preserve label separators or perform canonical mapping consistent with pool config. New runners should be accepted and assigned to pending jobs.

Immediate workaround tried:
- Manual re-assign of pending jobs to a healthy pool (manual override) — allowed one deploy to proceed.
- Rolled back runner token prefix normalization in a staging branch for testing (did not roll out to prod).

Logs & traces:
- Provisioner logs: /var/log/runner-provisioner/2026-03-12.log entries show successful registration events with token_meta: "rk_20260312_...".
- Scheduler logs (grep): "rejected_label_mismatch: runner_id=eu-3281 token_meta=rk_20260312".
- Kibana dashboard: https://kibana.redwood.ai/app/discover#/doc/ci-scheduler-logs/_search?query=rejected_label_mismatch

Notes on scope:
- Only pools that rely on exact slash-delimited label matching are affected (release/* pools). Other generic pools accept runners as expected.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: the vault rotation changed token format which triggers a legacy branch in label normalization (token_meta string contains underscore 'rk_' leading to fallback).
Hypothesis 2: recent change in runner-provisioner (infra PR 4218) added token metadata parsing that interacts with scheduler normalization.
Quick checks performed:
- Verified token strings in provisioner logs (confirmed 'rk_' prefix).
- Replayed normalization routine locally with sample token_meta: produced 'release-canary-v2' (slash removed).
- Reviewed PR 4218 — added token parsing but did not change label transformation; however, scheduler's normalization code (ci/scheduler) recently got a small refactor in PR 1192 that tightened validation.
Next steps in investigation:
- Add additional logging in scheduler label-normalizer to capture incoming runner labels and normalized output (temporary prod debug flag).
- Coordinate with infra on token rotation format to see if rotation job can emit compatibility header.
- Validate backlog of pending jobs and count how many can be assigned to alternative pools.
comments: 2026-03-12 03:02 - Dan Meyer (assignee): I've reproduced label mismatch locally using a copy of prod normalization code. It transforms '/' to '-' when token_meta contains underscore. Adding high priority. Linked infra PR 4218 for context.

2026-03-12 03:27 - Aisha Kapoor (SRE): Deployed debug logging to scheduler in us-east-1 (flag: scheduler.debug_label_norm=true). Seeing dozens of 'normalized_label=release-canary-v2' events right before rejections. Putting cluster into read-only for scheduled jobs to prevent further backlog growth.

2026-03-12 04:10 - Priya Nair (reporter): Confirming workaround of manual override worked to release canary-7. Customer teams informed via #release-ops slack. Will document which pipelines used manual assignment.

2026-03-12 07:45 - Dan Meyer: Temporary hotfix applied: relax strict label equality for release pools — scheduler now accepts either canonical slash form or dash-normalized form for the next 24 hours (feature flag). This allowed queued jobs to be assigned. Rolling this to stable after monitoring for 30m.

2026-03-13 09:12 - Infra Team (comment): Vault rotation job confirmed to have introduced 'rk_' prefix for rotated tokens starting 2026-03-12. We will add a compatibility header to rotation output. See PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4223.

2026-03-14 12:06 - Dan Meyer: Root cause analysis: interaction between vault token prefix and scheduler normalization logic introduced in ci/scheduler refactor (PR 1192). Patch merged to scheduler that normalizes labels consistently (PR 1198).

2026-03-14 12:45 - Dan Meyer: Resolution steps applied in prod: 1) apply label-normalizer patch (ci/scheduler PR 1198) 2) revert hotfix flag 3) verify queued jobs drained 4) coordinate follow-up to add integration test for token_metadata variations. Monitoring green for 24h.
2026-03-14 13:20 - Priya Nair: Closing customer communication loop. Notified Release Managers and created runbook follow-up items in Confluence.
2026-03-14 13:35 - Aisha Kapoor: Added follow-up task to add an alert for 'rejected_label_mismatch' spikes and updated runbook with manual override steps.
resolution: Fixed in prod by patching scheduler label-normalizer (ci/scheduler PR 1198) to canonicalize labels deterministically regardless of token_meta format. Hotfix acceptance tolerance was removed after verification. Backfilled 9 queued jobs via normal assignment. Added compatibility header to vault rotation output (infra PR 4223).
follow_up_actions: Add integration test for token metadata + label normalization (CI test suite)
Update runner-provisioner docs to document token metadata formats
Schedule retro with infra and release-eng to coordinate future rotations
